content.value: Lawyers, scientists, clinicians, dentists, and financial professionals share one demand no general-purpose document tool meets well: their documents must
prove

things. A brief pins its citations. A methods section carries a bibliography. A clinical note survives audit. A compliance memo shows where every figure came from. This paper designs the supply spine for those professions in Barkpark Papers: a citation and reference apparatus, a legal drafting toolkit, and a version-history record story told exactly as honestly as the code allows.

This is completion, not invention. Every primitive the evidence apparatus needs already has a live precedent in the engine — what is missing is one document-level pass, a small block family, and the discipline to claim no more than the database enforces.

content.value: One apparatus pass, a reference library, a legal toolkit, an honest record

Four pillars, in build order. The unifying insight of the investigation: everything derived — bibliographies from citations, numbering for figures, tables, equations, clauses and theorems, footnote markers, cross-reference labels, heading anchors — needs exactly
one document-level pre-render pass

, which the per-block compose pipeline cannot do today (compose.ex's own toc clause defers to a “document-level compose pass” that does not exist). The repo already holds the template for that pass three times over: TaskResolver (resolve/2 for readers plus preview/2 that never touches stored blocks), valueref resolution, and sheet hydration. One new resolver in the same shape serves lawyers (clauses), scientists (figures and bibliography), mathematicians (theorems), clinicians (guideline refs), and financial professionals (source-linked figures) at once.

content.value: Pillar 1 — references as first-class documents
A
type:"reference"
document stores one bibliographic source as CSL-JSON (the lingua franca Zotero, citeproc, Pandoc, and Crossref all speak). Import is one unauthenticated GET — the live probe against doi.org with the
application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json

Accept header returned a complete record (type, authors, container-title, volume, issue, pages, issued date, DOI, ISSN) with zero API keys. The snapshot is stored at import time so rendering stays offline and portable. Making references real documents — rather than block-local data — is what lets citations ride the existing graph: content_edges kinds are free strings (a new “cites” kind needs no migration), but to_id must be a real documents row, so external DOI/URL sources can only enter the graph as documents. That single choice buys the “cited by” reverse view for free on the reader's existing backlinks machinery, plus a personal library an individual scientist will recognize as Zotero-lite.
Pillar 2 — the apparatus pass
A new module in the TaskResolver shape — pure
resolve/2
for the reader plus a
preview/2

channel for the editor — walks the document once and: (a) resolves cite marks against the reference library, (b) derives the bibliography block's entries in the chosen style, (c) assigns numbers to figures, tables, equations, clauses, theorems, (d) resolves crossref marks into human labels — “Figure 3”, “Clause 4.2(b)”, “Section 2.1” — and (e) finally gives footnote its missing inline half: the shipped footnote block is a numbered list with fn-<id> anchors and no in-text markers, because the inline span was explicitly cut when the block was born (PR #4126). Formatting follows the math.ex doctrine: a bounded, deterministic CSL formatter for a fixed style set (APA, Vancouver, IEEE, Chicago, Harvard), honest degrade outside it — never an open citeproc plugin engine.
The pass must also build the landing pads the current cross-reference plumbing lacks. The storm's end-to-end probe returned a hard verdict: blockref anchors
DO NOT LAND

— walk.ex emits zero id attributes anywhere in its 1,565 lines (headings included), the anchor field is an opaque unvalidated author string, and the only id-bearing elements are the reader's stream wrappers (blocks-<block_id>), which exist only in block mode. Extending blockref therefore means building both ends: stable heading and figure anchors in the renderers, and an authoring surface in the editor (blockref and valueref marks are schema-only today — marks.js says so verbatim).

Derived artifacts — bibliography entries, numbers, resolved labels — must never leak into stored blocks. The canvas diffs on block bytes; a resolved snapshot entering the baseline persists stale rows and breaks byte-stability. TaskResolver's resolve/preview split (task_resolver.ex:54-88, doctrine D5/D3) exists precisely for this; the apparatus pass inherits it wholesale.

content.value: Pillar 4 — the record story, told honestly

The record-integrity audit came back stronger than expected in one direction and weaker in another. Stronger: revisions are not just append-only in app code — a real DB trigger (revisions_immutable) rejects direct UPDATE/DELETE with “revision history is append-only”, and a second trigger (revisions_bind_document) is what advances the current/released pointers. No pruning job exists anywhere (all 25 Oban workers enumerated). Weaker: the trigger deliberately lets cascaded deletes through — workspace deletion HARD-DELETES all revision and mutation_events history by documented design (tenancy.ex “class 2: just rows”) — mutation_events has no immutability trigger at all, and a failed revision insert is logged-and-swallowed, never aborting (the [revision-loss-silent] gap). Meanwhile audit_events is the codebase's actually tamper-evident table: an unconditional block trigger plus a sha256 hash chain.

content.value: The regulatory reality bounds the healthcare, dental and teacher claims: a US clinician collecting identified patient intake on a non-BAA cloud is in violation from the first record (45 CFR §160.103 / §164.502(e)); EU health data needs an Art. 9 basis plus an Art. 28 processing agreement; a teacher's NAMED gradebook on a personal account fails FERPA's direct-control test. The safe, shippable defaults are the anonymous, no-identifier shapes — patient-education handouts, anonymous polls — and any template that collects regulated personal data gets an explicit “this collects regulated data” flag. Solo lawyers, by contrast, are ALLOWED with reasonable-efforts diligence (ABA 477R/498) — the legal toolkit has no regulatory blocker, which is one reason it crowns well.

content.value: What we learned
The surprises, the corrections, and the premises that died under evidence:

items.value: Cross-references are broken at BOTH ends, not half-built. blockref renders /papers/<id>#<anchor> (walk.ex:811-825) but no element carries a matching id — walk.ex emits zero id attributes in 1,565 lines; headings get none (walk.ex:353-366); and no authoring UI exists (marks.js declares blockref/valueref SCHEMA-ONLY). The apparatus pass must build landing pads and triggers, not extend plumbing.

The footnote block shipped as half a feature: notes:[{id,text}] with fn-<id> anchors, the inline reference mark explicitly cut (PR #4126, “inline-span wiring out of scope”). No footnote-ref mark exists anywhere (zero grep hits). The inline side is where the cost lives — TipTap/convert.js round-tripping, not renderers.

A premise correction, twice over: the citation manager is NOT “an explicitly named gap” in the potential study (grep-disproven), AND this lane's own earlier claim that no citation wishlist entry exists was also wrong — the storm found B048 citation-list (B-tier, 3.05, “bibliography with inline cite markers — the academic apparatus”) beside B040 footnote (S-tier, built). The gap is real; its evidence is the block census and the wishlist ranking, not prior naming.

The record system is guarded by real DB triggers — a finding the lane had not yet read: revisions_immutable blocks direct UPDATE/DELETE; revisions_bind_document advances the pointers. But the guard has a designed cascade exception (workspace deletion erases history), and mutation_events has no trigger at all. audit_events — unconditional trigger plus sha256 chain — is the codebase's actual tamper-evidence precedent.

The export wall is absolute and load-bearing: no PDF generation, no docx in or out, no LaTeX anywhere — all grep-proven absences. What exists: a hand-tuned @media print stylesheet (bulldocs.html.heex:928, browser print-to-PDF only), a byte-exact email render (/papers/:slug/email), and the canonical JSON source endpoint. Sheets, by contrast, round-trips xlsx and exports five formats — the asymmetry caps every “export for the record” claim.

The anonymous form endpoint SHIPPED on origin/main mid-investigation (PR #5653): rate-limited, honeypotted, question-id-allowlisted, storing private form_response docs that fire webhooks and SSE for free — a webhook filtered to types:["form_response"] needs zero build. But forms have exactly five question types and NO signature, date, file, or required flag — consent forms need block work first, and the reader-side submit UI is a deliberate follow-up.

Every tool that does citations well (Word+Zotero, Overleaf, Typst) separates citation DATA from the DOCUMENT: a portable keyed store, with the document holding pointers resolved at render time. Every tool that does it badly (Notion: nothing; Craft/Obsidian: third-party bridges) lacks that separation. Google Docs and Word's built-ins are structured but siloed per-document. And nobody in the personal-tools class models a locator/pin-cite as a first-class field — that is the wedge.

The editor, not the renderer, is the scarcity: all 75 classified types have a dedicated TUI renderer and email has a designed twin or documented degrade for each — but only 33 types are human-insertable and 42 are unreachable, equation included. Any new evidence block must ship WITH its authoring surface or it joins the unreachable majority.

blocks.text: 05 · RISKS, UNKNOWNS, AND THE USER'S CALLS

content.value: Risks, unknowns, and the user's calls

Every new mark or block costs three emitters plus golden parity plus the editor round-trip — and the inline side (TipTap, convert.js) is the expensive half; the footnote team cut exactly that under the same pressure. The mitigation is the one-canonical-formatter option: Elixir formats citations, Go/TS render pre-formatted resolver strings. It halves the cost but breaks the every-surface-renders-from-source doctrine that equation upheld. The same tension surfaces in the notation and living-data lanes — one arbitration, at the capstone, for all three.

blocks.title: The triple-surface cost is real and front-loaded

content.value: A lawyer hands opposing counsel a file; a clinician files to a record system; both expect a document, not a URL. Today Papers offer browser print-to-PDF, a byte-exact email render, and JSON source — nothing programmatic. The evidence toolkit raises the value of closing this gap, but this lane does not design the exporter; it names the dependency so the capstone can weigh it.

blocks.title: No PDF/docx export caps the professional handoff

content.value: Judgment calls this Paper explicitly leaves to the user:

items.value: Reference library scope: per-paper self-containment (Overleaf's .bib model) vs a workspace-level shared library (the Zotero model). Both fit the type:"reference" design; the default changes the onboarding feel for an individual professional.
Formatter architecture: one canonical Elixir CSL formatter vs three parity twins — the run-wide doctrine tension; priced, undecided, capstone-bound.
The hash-chain upgrade: cheap tamper-evidence for revisions (the audit_events precedent) vs the compliance-adjacent overclaim it invites — marketing honesty is the real question, not engineering.
Legal citation v1: defer case-law citation entirely (recommended) vs build a separate bounded pin-cite formatter outside CSL.

Whether the apparatus wave pays the golden-regeneration cost of heading anchors + auto-TOC in the same PR (recommended: yes — crossrefs are broken without anchors) or splits it into a disarm-first wave.
Whether form-block consent shapes (signature, date, required) belong to this lane's build wave or to living-data-forms — the “collects regulated data” flag design must be shared either way.

The Evidence Apparatus — citations, redlines, and records for the trust professions

Lawyers, scientists, clinicians, dentists, and financial professionals share one demand no general-purpose document tool meets well: their documents must prove things. A brief pins its citations. A methods section carries a bibliography. A clinical note survives audit. A compliance memo shows where every figure came from. This paper designs the supply spine for those professions in Barkpark Papers: a citation and reference apparatus, a legal drafting toolkit, and a version-history record story told exactly as honestly as the code allows.

This is completion, not invention. Every primitive the evidence apparatus needs already has a live precedent in the engine — what is missing is one document-level pass, a small block family, and the discipline to claim no more than the database enforces.

01 · WHAT WE WILL CREATE

One apparatus pass, a reference library, a legal toolkit, an honest record

Four pillars, in build order. The unifying insight of the investigation: everything derived — bibliographies from citations, numbering for figures, tables, equations, clauses and theorems, footnote markers, cross-reference labels, heading anchors — needs exactly one document-level pre-render pass, which the per-block compose pipeline cannot do today (compose.ex's own toc clause defers to a “document-level compose pass” that does not exist). The repo already holds the template for that pass three times over: TaskResolver (resolve/2 for readers plus preview/2 that never touches stored blocks), valueref resolution, and sheet hydration. One new resolver in the same shape serves lawyers (clauses), scientists (figures and bibliography), mathematicians (theorems), clinicians (guideline refs), and financial professionals (source-linked figures) at once.

Pillar 1 — references as first-class documents

A type:"reference" document stores one bibliographic source as CSL-JSON (the lingua franca Zotero, citeproc, Pandoc, and Crossref all speak). Import is one unauthenticated GET — the live probe against doi.org with the application/vnd.citationstyles.csl+json Accept header returned a complete record (type, authors, container-title, volume, issue, pages, issued date, DOI, ISSN) with zero API keys. The snapshot is stored at import time so rendering stays offline and portable. Making references real documents — rather than block-local data — is what lets citations ride the existing graph: content_edges kinds are free strings (a new “cites” kind needs no migration), but to_id must be a real documents row, so external DOI/URL sources can only enter the graph as documents. That single choice buys the “cited by” reverse view for free on the reader's existing backlinks machinery, plus a personal library an individual scientist will recognize as Zotero-lite.

{
  "id": "smith2024",                       // stable cite key
  "type": "article-journal",               // CSL type vocabulary
  "title": "...",
  "author": [{"family": "Smith", "given": "Jane"}],
  "container-title": "Nature",
  "volume": "500", "issue": "7460", "page": "54-58",
  "issued": {"date-parts": [[2024, 5, 14]]},
  "DOI": "...", "URL": "..."
}

// inline cite MARK carried on text — the lawyer's pin-cite and the
// scientist's page-cite share one shape (no personal tool models this)
{"type": "cite", "ref": "smith2024",
 "locator": "45", "locator_label": "page",   // or "§3.2" / "fig. 3"
 "prefix": "see"}                            // legal signal, optional

// bibliography block — DERIVED at render time, never stored resolved
{"type": "bibliography", "style": "apa"}     // apa|vancouver|ieee|chicago|harvard

Pillar 2 — the apparatus pass

A new module in the TaskResolver shape — pure resolve/2 for the reader plus a preview/2 channel for the editor — walks the document once and: (a) resolves cite marks against the reference library, (b) derives the bibliography block's entries in the chosen style, (c) assigns numbers to figures, tables, equations, clauses, theorems, (d) resolves crossref marks into human labels — “Figure 3”, “Clause 4.2(b)”, “Section 2.1” — and (e) finally gives footnote its missing inline half: the shipped footnote block is a numbered list with fn-<id> anchors and no in-text markers, because the inline span was explicitly cut when the block was born (PR #4126). Formatting follows the math.ex doctrine: a bounded, deterministic CSL formatter for a fixed style set (APA, Vancouver, IEEE, Chicago, Harvard), honest degrade outside it — never an open citeproc plugin engine.

The pass must also build the landing pads the current cross-reference plumbing lacks. The storm's end-to-end probe returned a hard verdict: blockref anchors DO NOT LAND — walk.ex emits zero id attributes anywhere in its 1,565 lines (headings included), the anchor field is an opaque unvalidated author string, and the only id-bearing elements are the reader's stream wrappers (blocks-<block_id>), which exist only in block mode. Extending blockref therefore means building both ends: stable heading and figure anchors in the renderers, and an authoring surface in the editor (blockref and valueref marks are schema-only today — marks.js says so verbatim).

The one law the design must never break Derived artifacts — bibliography entries, numbers, resolved labels — must never leak into stored blocks. The canvas diffs on block bytes; a resolved snapshot entering the baseline persists stale rows and breaks byte-stability. TaskResolver's resolve/preview split (task_resolver.ex:54-88, doctrine D5/D3) exists precisely for this; the apparatus pass inherits it wholesale.

Pillar 3 — the legal toolkit

Grounded in what practicing tools actually do (Clio Draft, Lexis Create+, Litera, Definely), the credible v1 for an individual lawyer is three capabilities — none of which require Word interop:

Clause numbering + cross-refsclause blocks numbered by the apparatus pass (decimal 1.1.1 and outline 1(a)(i) modes); crossref marks resolve to “Clause 4.2(b)” and survive renumberingthe same numbering engine as figures and equations

Redline v1revision-compare: word-level prose diff between two paper revisions, rendered ins/del on all three surfaces — read-only, honest, cheaprevisions are append-only snapshots; the existing diff BLOCK is the wrong primitive (verbatim unified diff for code)

Phase 2, explicitly deferred: extending the Proposals loop (papers/proposals.ex — insert-only agent suggestions with mandatory provenance, reviewed through the draft→publish gate) into reviewable mutating ops — true tracked changes with per-span author, timestamp and accept/reject. That is a new state machine the proposals module deliberately refused; it must be earned, not assumed. One-way export of a native redline to OOXML w:ins/w:del (so a counterparty opens it in Word) is realistic later; two-way Word redline round-trip is Litera Compare's entire moat and is explicitly out.

Bluebook is not CSL-servable — say so A bluebook-law-review.csl style exists, but CSL's architecture structurally cannot do supra/short-form citation tracking or first-page extraction — core Bluebook conventions the CSL maintainer refused outright. Legal v1 ships clause + defined-term + redline and defers case-law citation formatting entirely (or ships a separate bounded pin-cite formatter later). It must never promise Bluebook fidelity through the CSL path that serves scientists.

Pillar 4 — the record story, told honestly

The record-integrity audit came back stronger than expected in one direction and weaker in another. Stronger: revisions are not just append-only in app code — a real DB trigger (revisions_immutable) rejects direct UPDATE/DELETE with “revision history is append-only”, and a second trigger (revisions_bind_document) is what advances the current/released pointers. No pruning job exists anywhere (all 25 Oban workers enumerated). Weaker: the trigger deliberately lets cascaded deletes through — workspace deletion HARD-DELETES all revision and mutation_events history by documented design (tenancy.ex “class 2: just rows”) — mutation_events has no immutability trigger at all, and a failed revision insert is logged-and-swallowed, never aborting (the [revision-loss-silent] gap). Meanwhile audit_events is the codebase's actually tamper-evident table: an unconditional block trigger plus a sha256 hash chain.

The regulatory reality bounds the healthcare, dental and teacher claims: a US clinician collecting identified patient intake on a non-BAA cloud is in violation from the first record (45 CFR §160.103 / §164.502(e)); EU health data needs an Art. 9 basis plus an Art. 28 processing agreement; a teacher's NAMED gradebook on a personal account fails FERPA's direct-control test. 05 · RISKS, UNKNOWNS, AND THE USER'S CALLS

Risks, unknowns, and the user's calls

The triple-surface cost is real and front-loaded Every new mark or block costs three emitters plus golden parity plus the editor round-trip — and the inline side (TipTap, convert.js) is the expensive half; the footnote team cut exactly that under the same pressure. The mitigation is the one-canonical-formatter option: Elixir formats citations, Go/TS render pre-formatted resolver strings. It halves the cost but breaks the every-surface-renders-from-source doctrine that equation upheld. The same tension surfaces in the notation and living-data lanes — one arbitration, at the capstone, for all three.
No PDF/docx export caps the professional handoff A lawyer hands opposing counsel a file; a clinician files to a record system; both expect a document, not a URL. Today Papers offer browser print-to-PDF, a byte-exact email render, and JSON source — nothing programmatic. The evidence toolkit raises the value of closing this gap, but this lane does not design the exporter; it names the dependency so the capstone can weigh it.

Judgment calls this Paper explicitly leaves to the user:

  1. Reference library scope: per-paper self-containment (Overleaf's .bib model) vs a workspace-level shared library (the Zotero model). Both fit the type:"reference" design; the default changes the onboarding feel for an individual professional.
  2. Formatter architecture: one canonical Elixir CSL formatter vs three parity twins — the run-wide doctrine tension; priced, undecided, capstone-bound.
  3. The hash-chain upgrade: cheap tamper-evidence for revisions (the audit_events precedent) vs the compliance-adjacent overclaim it invites — marketing honesty is the real question, not engineering.
  4. Legal citation v1: defer case-law citation entirely (recommended) vs build a separate bounded pin-cite formatter outside CSL.
  5. Whether the apparatus wave pays the golden-regeneration cost of heading anchors + auto-TOC in the same PR (recommended: yes — crossrefs are broken without anchors) or splits it into a disarm-first wave.
  6. Whether form-block consent shapes (signature, date, required) belong to this lane's build wave or to living-data-forms — the “collects regulated data” flag design must be shared either way.
